messages:
Jordan: Customer BrightBridge reporting sustained 429s for their dedicated endpoint during a traffic spike. They say the dedicated pool didn’t scale past min replicas. Customer on the phone now. Link to convo: https://intercom.example/conv/BB-1123 :telephone_receiver:
Anita: Got the account. Repro from customer: repeated requests to /v1/generate -> many 429s after ~20s queueing. They shared a curl script: 
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -sS -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-dedicated-1","input":"hi"}'; done
```
Jordan: They ran that at ~11:05 PDT and traffic jumped. Support logs show request queue depth climbing then 429s. Attaching excerpt: `queue_len: 120, avg_wait_ms: 21500, 429_rate: 0.32`
Devon: Looking at autoscaler metrics now. The autoscaler saw increased incoming_rps but scale_decision stayed at 0 for ~2m. Query: `sum(rate(req_in[1m])) by (tenant) / desired_qps` shows BrightBridge underpredicted headroom. I suspect the request rate metric used for scale decisions is being downsampled due to our new ingestion window.
Maya: Pulled autoscaler logs for their tenant: 
```
[2026-03-16T18:05:12Z] tenant=brightbridge scale_eval: observed_rps=240 target_per_replica=200 desired=2 current=2 decision=NO_SCALE reason=estimated_headroom=160
[2026-03-16T18:06:30Z] tenant=brightbridge provisioning: attempt_start pod_create_pending: image_pull_backoff
```
Leo: Node kubelet logs from cluster show repeated image pull 429s from our private registry: `rpc error: code = Unknown desc = toomanyrequests: Rate exceeded` — looks like registry rate limiting delayed pod readiness by ~70s for each new replica. That explains scale delay, not autoscaler logic alone.
Sam: Cross-checking billing/auth: customer billing is OK. However, our registry token rotation for internal push mirror to cache in us-west-2 failed for a short window (rotated keys not distributed). So when pods tried to pull, they hit the upstream and ran into rate caps. ops-bot: creating incident.
ops-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-1043 | brightbridge-dedicated-scaleup-stall | priority=P2 | owner=Devon
Anita: Customer wants immediate mitigation. Can we manually bump min_replicas for BrightBridge so existing pods can absorb traffic while we fix pulls?
Devon: I can bump min_replicas to 3 temporarily. Command: `redwoodctl capacity update --tenant brightbridge --min-replicas 3` Doing it now.
Maya: After bump, I see new pods started but many were stuck in ImagePullBackOff initially, then gradually became Running as mirror cache warmed. Metrics post-change: `queue_len` dropped from 120 -> 8 within 90s and 429s dropped to 0.06.
Leo: Long-term fix: add registry client-side caching + exponential backoff and retry for image pulls in our node bootstrap, and ensure token rotation is staged across mirrors. Also add autoscaler tie-breaker to prefer scale_out_when_pending_pods>0.
Sam: Noting customer impact and proposing a one-time credit. CS to follow up.
Jordan: Customer on call confirmed latencies improved after ~3m and 429s mostly stopped. They want postmortem and root cause.
Devon: Ownering a short postmortem and a config change PR to: (1) reduce autoscaler downsample window, (2) make registry mirror token rollout atomic, (3) add scale override when image pull backlog present.
Anita: Repro steps for on-call: 1) run the curl spike above; 2) watch `kubectl get pods -l tenant=brightbridge -w`; 3) monitor metric `autoscaler.pending_pods{tenant=brightbridge}` and `node.image_pull_errors`; 4) if stuck, run `redwoodctl capacity update --tenant brightbridge --min-replicas 3`.
Maya: Adding alerts to paging: if pending_pods>5 for >30s during spike, page eng-platform.
Jordan: Marking incident resolved for now — customer recovered and CS is scheduling follow-up. Closing thread once postmortem link is posted. :white_check_mark:
